s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual field defect with worsening headaches and a history of intracerebral hemorrhage
salient_findings: Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old Asian man
4-month history of worsening headaches
Complete right homonymous hemianopia
History of left occipital intracerebral hematoma of unknown cause 2 years earlier
Normal vital signs
Neurologic testing confirmed visual field defect without other focal deficits
Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI
Subtotal removal of the mass during left occipital craniotomy
Intraoperative finding of the mass invading the falx cerebri and adjacent cortex
Postoperative CT showed no complications
Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and high mitotic activity, consistent with hemangiopericytoma

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemical studies showed strong immunoreactivity for CD99, a marker often expressed in solitary fibrous tumors

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's location and invasion of the falx cerebri and adjacent cortex are consistent with meningioma, although histopathological features are not typical

shortlist.label: Cavernous angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial imaging suggested a cavernous angioma, but histopathological examination did not support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: The high mitotic activity and invasive behavior of the tumor raise concern for a malignant solitary fibrous tumor

raw.rationale: The histopathological examination showing spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1 is consistent with Hemangiopericytoma, a rare vascular tumor that can present with hemorrhage and has a tendency to invade surrounding structures.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: While solitary fibrous tumors can show similar immunohistochemical profiles, the presence of up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields and the clinical presentation with hemorrhage are less typical for this entity.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Meningiomas typically have a distinct histological appearance with whorling patterns and psammoma bodies, which are not described in this case, and they usually do not exhibit such high mitotic activity.

rejected.label: Cavernous angioma
rejected.why: The initial suspicion of a cavernous angioma based on imaging was not supported by the histopathological findings, which did not show the characteristic multicystic appearance of cavernous angiomas.

rejected.label: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: Although the tumor shows some features that could suggest malignancy, such as a high mitotic rate, the overall histological and immunohistochemical profile is more consistent with Hemangiopericytoma, which can also exhibit aggressive behavior.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor is less likely due to the high mitotic rate and the specific immunohistochemical profile
rejected.why: The high mitotic rate and specific immunohistochemical profile are more consistent with Hemangiopericytoma
